source.title: Results and Open Questions on the Boundary Control of Moving Sets

accepted.question_text: Consider a controlled system of reaction-diffusion equations for n interacting populations, with state u=(u_1,…,u_n), control α(x)∈R^m, diffusion coefficients σ_i, and traveling-wave profiles U=(U_1,…,U_n) of speed β that connect two asymptotically stable equilibria u^- and u^+. Among all controls that produce such a traveling wave, one wants to minimize the total running cost ∫_{-∞}^{+∞} L(U(x),α(x)) dx. Develop a fully general theory for this multi-population optimal traveling-wave problem: establish general conditions under which optimal controls and profiles exist, and derive corresponding necessary conditions for optimality.

evidence.quote: In the above setting, the cost functional does not admit the convenient representation (2.12). A fully general theory for this type of optimization problems is not yet available. Under suitable assumptions on the functions f and L, one can prove the existence of optimal solutions, and derive necessary conditions for optimality.

accepted.question_text: Let t→Ω(t)⊂R^2 be a moving set with C^1 boundary and inward normal speed β(t,x)≥β*. Suppose there are controls α^ε≥0 and solutions u^ε of the rescaled reaction-diffusion equation u_t^ε=(1/ε)f(u^ε)+εΔu^ε-αu^ε such that u^ε(t,·) converges in L^1 to the indicator function 1_{Ω(t)} for every t∈[0,T]. Must the control costs satisfy the lower bound lim inf_{ε→0} ∫_{R^2} α^ε(t,x) dx ≥ ∫_{∂Ω(t)} E(β(t,x)) dσ? Equivalently, can one prove the converse inequality needed to justify the moving-set cost functional as a Γ-limit of the rescaled parabolic control costs?

evidence.quote: In view of these results, one may speculate if it is possible to regard the cost functional J as a Γ-limit of the functionals J^ε. Toward this goal, one would need a converse to Theorem 3.1.

Question 1: In the same setting of Theorem 3.1, consider any family of control functions α^ε ≥ 0 and corresponding solutions u^ε to (3.6) such that (3.7) holds. Does this imply that lim inf_{ε→0} ∫_{R2} α^ε(t, x) dx ≥ ∫_{∂Ω(t)} E(β(t, x)) dσ ? (3.10)

accepted.question_text: For the optimal set motion problem (OSM), Theorem 4.1 gives existence of optimal solutions in a very general class of sets with finite perimeter, while the Pontryagin-type necessary conditions in Section 5 require much stronger regularity. Prove regularity of an optimal set-valued map t→Ω(t) solving (OSM) that is strong enough to justify those necessary conditions; in particular, prove that the orthogonal trajectories to the moving boundaries ∂Ω(t) are well defined.

evidence.quote: At this stage, we must point out that a major gap still remains in the theory. Indeed, Theorem 4.1 yields the existence of optimal solutions t 7→ Ω(t) within a general class of sets with finite perimeter. On the other hand, the necessary conditions require a much stronger regularity assumption.
Problem 2. Establish the regularity of the set valued map t 7→ Ω(t) which provides a solution to (OSM). In particular, prove that the orthogonal curves to the boundaries ∂Ω(t) are well defined.

accepted.question_text: Let V⊂R^2 be an open connected domain with bounded perimeter, and consider the constrained eradication problem (CEP) for moving contaminated sets Ω(t)⊆V under the boundary-effort constraint described in Section 6. Determine the strategy t→Ω(t) that eradicates the contamination in minimum time for a general such domain V. In particular, characterize the optimal strategy when V is a polygon and when V is a convex domain with smooth boundary.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, there are many domains V ⊂ R2 for which the conditions in Theorem 7.2 are not satisfied by any map t 7→ Ω(t) ⊆ V . For example, think of a triangle. Another example is shown in Fig. 20, left. This leads to our third main open problem:

Problem 3. Given an open connected domain V ⊂ R2 with bounded perimeter, describe the optimal strategy t 7→ Ω(t) ⊆ V for (CEP), achieving the eradication in minimum time. In particular, it would be of interest to study the cases where (i) V is a polygon, or (ii) V is a convex set with smooth boundary.

accepted.question_text: Let V⊂R^2 be a compact connected set of area A, and consider the optimal slicing problem: construct a nested family of subsets Ω(t)⊆V for t∈[0,A] such that m_2(Ω(t))=t and Ω(t_1)⊂Ω(t_2) whenever 0≤t_1<t_2≤A, while minimizing the average relative-boundary length ∫_0^A m_1(V∩∂Ω(t)) dt. Determine the optimal slicing in geometries like the domain shown in Figure 20, where the sufficient conditions from Theorem 7.2 do not apply.

evidence.quote: (OSP) (Optimal slicing problem). Let V ⊂ R2 be a compact connected set with m2(V ) = A > 0. Construct a family of sets t 7→ Ω(t) ⊆ V whose relative boundaries minimize the integral ∫ A 0 m1(V ∩ ∂Ω(t)) dt, subject to m2(Ω(t)) = t, for all t ∈ [0, A], Ω(t1) ⊂ Ω(t2), for 0 ≤ t1 < t2 ≤ A.
It remains an open problem to understand the optimal slicing of a set such as the one in Fig. 20.
